call_tech: The code persists after filters are clean and pressure is normal
Water is leaking at the inlet valve or hose connection
The valve hums or buzzes but no water enters
You are not comfortable disconnecting hoses
causes: A water supply tap that is closed or only partly open
A kinked, squashed or blocked inlet hose
A clogged mesh filter where the hose meets the inlet valve
Low household water pressure
A frozen inlet hose in cold weather
A faulty water inlet valve (less common)
checks: Confirm both hot and cold taps are fully open
Look along both inlet hoses for kinks or crushing
Check whether another tap in the house runs normally, to judge pressure
Look at the mesh filters inside the inlet valve connections for grit or debris

faqs.a: Usually not. In most cases it is a closed tap, a kinked hose, or a dirty inlet filter — all of which you can check in a few minutes.
faqs.q: Is IE always a serious fault?

faqs.a: Yes. If the house pressure is very low, the washer may time out before it fills. Check another tap: if that is also slow, the problem is in the household supply, not the washer.
faqs.q: Can low water pressure cause IE?

codes.meaning: The washer is not receiving enough water within the time it expects. The cycle usually stops before washing properly begins, because there is too little water in the drum to wash with.
codes.reset: A power cycle (unplug for a minute, then plug back in) clears a one-off glitch, but it does not fix a blocked filter or a closed tap. If IE returns straight away, the underlying cause is still present.
codes.safety: Unplug the machine and turn the taps off before disconnecting any hose. Water and electricity do not mix — mop up spills before restoring power.

sources.label: LG washing machine error code guides (independent, cross-checked)
LG washing machine troubleshooting codes guide

steps: Switch the washer off and unplug it, and turn both supply taps off before you touch any hose.
Turn both taps fully on again and check the pressure at a nearby tap.
Straighten any kinked inlet hose and make sure it is not squashed behind the machine.
Disconnect each inlet hose (keep a towel ready), remove the small mesh filter at the valve end, rinse it clean with an old toothbrush, and refit it.
Reconnect the hoses firmly, turn the taps on, plug in, and run a short cycle.
If the code returns with clean filters and good pressure, the inlet valve itself is the likely fault.
codes.title: Water inlet error — the washer is not filling

call_tech: The code persists with a clean filter and a clear hose
The drain pump makes no sound at all, or hums loudly without pumping
Water leaks from the pump area
You cannot reach or open the pump filter
causes: A kinked or blocked drain hose
A clogged drain pump filter (lint, coins, small objects)
A drain hose positioned too high, or its end submerged in standing water
Too much detergent creating excess suds that slow draining
A faulty drain pump
checks: Look along the drain hose for kinks or crushing
Check the pump filter at the bottom front of the machine for debris
Check the drain hose height and that its end is not sitting in water
Look for excessive foam in the drum

faqs.a: Not while water is in the drum — front-load doors stay locked for safety. Drain through the pump filter first, then the door should release.
faqs.q: Can I open the door when OE is showing?

faqs.a: Yes, indirectly. Excess suds slow the pump and can trip the drain timeout, especially with non-HE detergent in an HE machine.
faqs.q: Does too much detergent really cause OE?

codes.meaning: Water is not leaving the drum within the time the washer expects. The machine usually stops with water still sitting in the drum, and the spin may not run.
codes.reset: A power cycle clears a one-off glitch, but it cannot clear a blocked filter or hose. If OE returns on the next cycle, the blockage or pump fault is still there.
codes.safety: Unplug before opening the pump filter. Expect a litre or more of water — work slowly and keep the area dry before restoring power.

sources.label: LG washing machine error code guides (independent, cross-checked)
LG washing machine troubleshooting codes guide

steps: Switch off and unplug the machine. Keep towels and a shallow tray ready — water will come out of the filter.
Open the pump filter cover, drain the remaining water slowly, then remove and clean the filter.
Check the drain hose along its full length for kinks, and confirm it is routed correctly with no sagging loops full of water.
If there are heavy suds, run a rinse-only cycle with no detergent to clear them.
Refit the filter firmly, plug in, and run a drain or spin cycle.
If the pump hums but nothing drains, or the code returns with a clean filter and a clear hose, the pump is the likely fault.
codes.title: Drain error — the washer is not draining

call_tech: UE appears with normal, balanced, everyday loads
The drum bangs loudly even when the load is even
The machine has moved across the floor or its feet are damaged
causes: One heavy item (a blanket, bathrobe, or pair of jeans) on its own
Heavy and light items mixed together
Too small a load to spread around the drum
A machine that is not level, so loads always settle to one side
checks: Pause the machine and look at how the load is sitting
Check whether the machine rocks when you push its corners
Note whether the code appears with one particular item or with every load

faqs.a: Lowercase uE means the washer is still attempting to rebalance the load itself. Uppercase UE means it could not rebalance and stopped for you to fix the load.
faqs.q: What is the difference between uE and UE?

faqs.a: A single heavy item cannot spread around the drum, so one side is always heavier. Adding a couple of towels gives the drum something to balance against.
faqs.q: Why does one blanket always cause UE?

codes.meaning: The laundry inside the drum is unevenly distributed, so the machine cannot spin safely. A lowercase uE means the washer is still trying to rebalance the load on its own; an uppercase UE means it has given up and needs your help.
codes.reset: No reset is needed for UE. It is not a fault — it is the machine protecting itself from a violent spin. Fix the load and the code clears.
codes.safety: Never open the door mid-spin. Wait for the drum to stop completely before reaching inside.

sources.label: LG washing machine error code guides (independent, cross-checked)
LG washing machine reset and codes guide

steps: Pause the cycle and wait for the door to unlock.
Redistribute the laundry evenly around the drum — untangle sheets and spread heavy items out.
For a single heavy item, add two or three towels to balance it.
Close the door and restart the spin.
If the machine rocks, adjust its feet until it stands firm and level, then retry.
codes.title: Unbalanced load — the drum cannot spin evenly

call_tech: LE returns with normal, everyday loads
The drum will not turn by hand, or grinds
There is a burning smell
The code appears even with an empty drum
causes: An overloaded drum
A foreign object caught between the drum and the tub
A motor or sensor fault (less common)
checks: How full is the drum? It should never be packed tight
Turn the drum slowly by hand (machine off) and feel for grinding or catching
Look for small items trapped at the door seal

faqs.a: No. On LG washers LE means a locked or overloaded motor. On some other brands the same letters can mean something different — always check the code for your brand and model.
faqs.q: Is LE the same on every brand?

faqs.a: About 30 minutes, to let the motor cool. Restarting immediately after an overload trip can trip it again.
faqs.q: How long should I wait before retrying?

codes.meaning: The motor is drawing too much current, usually because the drum is overloaded or something is stopping it from turning freely. The machine stops to protect the motor.
codes.reset: LE often clears after the motor cools and the load is reduced. If it returns immediately with a normal load, do not keep restarting — the motor or its sensor needs checking.
codes.safety: Unplug before reaching into the drum or checking for trapped objects. Never bypass a motor protection trip — it is there to prevent overheating.

sources.label: LG washing machine error code guides (independent, cross-checked)
LG washing machine troubleshooting codes guide

steps: Switch off and unplug the machine.
Remove some of the laundry so the drum is no more than about three-quarters full.
Check around the door seal and, if you can, between drum and tub for trapped objects.
Let the motor cool for about 30 minutes.
Plug in and restart with the smaller load.
codes.title: Locked motor error — the motor is overloaded

call_tech: The latch is visibly broken or the door will not stay shut
The code persists with a clean seal and a firmly closed door
The door lock makes repeated clicking sounds without locking
causes: Laundry caught in the door seal
The door not pushed fully shut
A misaligned door or a faulty door latch / interlock
checks: Look around the rubber door seal for trapped clothing
Push the door firmly and listen for the latch click
Check the latch area for visible damage

faqs.a: They are sub-variants of the same door fault family: the door is open, or the lock mechanism is not engaging. The checks are the same — start with obstructions and a firm close.
faqs.q: What do dE1 and dE2 mean?

faqs.a: Yes, if the seal stops the door from sitting square in the frame. A seal that is folded, torn, or swollen with detergent residue can prevent latching.
faqs.q: Can a worn door seal cause dE?

codes.meaning: The door (or lid) is not fully closed, or the door lock is not engaging. The machine will not start or continue a cycle until the door is properly latched.
codes.reset: A power cycle does not fix a door error. The latch must engage — if it cannot, the part needs attention.
codes.safety: Never force the door while the drum is spinning, and never defeat the door lock — it prevents the drum from opening mid-cycle.

sources.label: LG washing machine error code guides (independent, cross-checked)
LG washing machine troubleshooting codes guide

steps: Pause or switch off the machine.
Open the door, remove anything caught in the seal, and check the seal sits flat.
Close the door firmly until it latches.
Restart the cycle.
If the code stays with a clean, firmly closed door, the latch or interlock is the likely fault.
codes.title: Door error — the door is not closed or latched

call_tech: 4E persists with the tap open, good pressure, and clean filters
The inlet valve leaks or makes no sound when it should be filling
You are not comfortable disconnecting hoses
causes: A water supply tap that is closed
Low household water pressure
A kinked inlet hose
Clogged mesh filters at the water hose connections
checks: Confirm the supply tap is fully open
Check the water pressure at another tap
Look for kinks in the inlet hose
Check the mesh filters for debris

faqs.a: They are the same fault. Samsung renamed the code on newer models: older machines show 4E, newer ones show 4C. The checks are identical.
faqs.q: What is the difference between 4E and 4C?

faqs.a: On this fault the washer first drains for about 3 minutes as a safety step. Wait for the drain to finish; the controls respond again after that.
faqs.q: Why does the Power button not respond when 4E shows?

codes.meaning: The washer is not getting water, or not enough of it. Newer Samsung models show the same fault as 4C. The machine stops the wash because it cannot fill the drum.
codes.reset: A power cycle clears a one-off glitch, but a closed tap, kinked hose, or dirty filter will bring 4E straight back. Fix the supply first.
codes.safety: Unplug and turn the taps off before disconnecting any hose. Dry up spills before restoring power.

sources.label: Samsung washing machine user manual — information codes table
Samsung washing machine user manual (WF8800JSS) — information codes

steps: Make sure the source water tap is turned on.
Check the water pressure — if another tap is also slow, the household supply is the problem.
Straighten the inlet hose and remove any kinking.
Clean the mesh filters of the water hose (rinse out grit and debris).
Restart the cycle. Note: when 4E shows, the washer first drains for about 3 minutes, during which the Power button does not respond — wait for that to finish.
codes.title: Water supply error — the washer is not filling

call_tech: 5E persists with a clean filter and a correctly routed hose
The pump is silent or hums without draining
Water leaks from the pump or hose connections
causes: A blocked debris filter
A drain hose installed incorrectly, kinked, or blocked
A clogged water hose mesh filter (listed in Samsung's own checks for this code)
A drain pump fault
checks: Look at the debris filter for lint, coins, and small objects
Check the drain hose routing, height, and any kinks
Listen for the drain pump running during the drain step

faqs.a: They are the same fault. Older Samsung machines show 5E; newer ones show 5C. The checks are identical.
faqs.q: What is the difference between 5E and 5C?

faqs.a: On most Samsung front-load washers it is behind a small cover at the bottom front of the machine. Your model's manual shows the exact location.
faqs.q: Where is the debris filter?

codes.meaning: The washer cannot drain water from the drum. Newer Samsung models show the same fault as 5C. The cycle stops with water left in the drum.
codes.reset: A power cycle clears a one-off glitch only. If 5E returns, the filter, hose, or pump still needs attention.
codes.safety: Unplug before opening the filter. Water will spill — work slowly and dry the area before restoring power.

sources.label: Samsung washing machine user manual — information codes table
Samsung washing machine user manual (WF8800JSS) — information codes

steps: Switch off and unplug the machine, with towels and a tray ready.
Clean the debris filter thoroughly.
Make sure the drainage hose is installed correctly — no kinks, no sagging loops, and the end positioned as the manual requires.
Clean the water hose mesh filter as well.
Refit everything firmly and run a drain or spin cycle.
codes.title: Drain error — the washer is not draining

call_tech: UE appears with normal, balanced, everyday loads
The drum bangs violently even when the load is even
The machine has moved across the floor
causes: A single heavy item washed alone
Laundry bunched to one side of the drum
Very small loads that cannot spread around the drum
checks: Pause and look at how the load is sitting
Check whether the code follows one particular item
Check the machine stands level and does not rock

faqs.a: Because a single heavy, absorbent item is the classic trigger: it soaks up water, gets very heavy, and cannot spread around the drum on its own.
faqs.q: Why does Samsung mention bathrobes and jeans specifically?

faqs.a: The meaning is the same — an unbalanced load — but the machines are different, so always follow the steps for your own brand and model.
faqs.q: Is Samsung UE the same as LG UE?

codes.meaning: The laundry load is unbalanced, so the washer cannot spin it safely. Samsung's own manual notes that washing a single item — such as a bathrobe or a pair of jeans — commonly ends with this message, and the final spin result may be unsatisfactory.
codes.reset: No reset is needed. UE is the machine protecting itself from an uneven spin. Fix the load and the code clears.
codes.safety: Wait for the drum to stop completely before opening the door.

sources.label: Samsung washing machine user manual — information codes table
Samsung washing machine user manual (WF8800JSS) — information codes

steps: Pause the cycle and wait for the door to unlock.
Redistribute the load evenly around the drum.
For a single heavy item, add a few towels to balance it.
Close the door and restart the spin.
codes.title: Unbalanced load — the drum cannot spin evenly

call_tech: The latch is broken or the door will not stay shut
The code persists with a clean seal and a firmly closed door
causes: Laundry caught in the door or seal
The door not pushed fully shut
A faulty door latch (less common)
checks: Look around the door and seal for trapped clothing
Push the door firmly and listen for the latch
Check the latch area for damage

faqs.a: The meaning is the same — a door that is not closed or latched — but always follow your own brand's manual for the exact checks.
faqs.q: Is Samsung dE the same as LG dE?

codes.meaning: The door is not firmly closed, or laundry is caught in it, so the door lock cannot engage. The washer will not run until the door is properly shut.
codes.reset: A power cycle does not fix a door error — the latch must engage. If it cannot, the latch needs attention.
codes.safety: Never force the door while the drum is moving, and never defeat the door lock.

sources.label: Samsung washing machine user manual — information codes table
Samsung washing machine user manual (WF8800JSS) — information codes

steps: Pause or switch off the machine.
Open the door and remove anything caught in it.
Check the seal sits flat, then close the door firmly.
Restart the cycle.
codes.title: Door error — the door is not firmly closed

call_tech: E15 returns after the tray is drained and dried
You can see water dripping but cannot find the source
The float switch or inlet valve is suspected
The machine is built in and you cannot safely reach the base
causes: A small leak from a hose, seal, or the sump area
A stuck or faulty float switch
A water inlet valve that does not shut fully
Over-foaming that pushes water out of the tub
checks: Look under and around the machine for visible water
Check the inlet hose and drain hose connections for drips
Check the door seal for damage or trapped debris

faqs.a: Because resetting does not repair the leak. The tray refills from the same drip, the float lifts again, and E15 returns. Find the drip first.
faqs.q: Why does E15 keep coming back after I reset it?

faqs.a: No. Repeated tray water means an ongoing leak. Apart from floor damage, running the machine this way risks electrical damage.
faqs.q: Can I just keep draining the tray?

codes.meaning: Water has collected in the base tray underneath the dishwasher, lifting the safety float switch. The machine stops the water supply and pauses the cycle to protect your floor. E15 means there is a real leak (or a stuck float) — not a software glitch.
codes.reset: A reset or a drained tray only buys time. If the tray refills, the code will come back — the leak, valve, or float is still faulty. Do not keep resetting and running the machine with an active leak.
codes.safety: Unplug before touching anything wet, and keep the water supply off until the leak is found. Never run a dishwasher with an active leak — water damage spreads fast, and water plus electrics is dangerous.

sources.label: Bosch dishwasher E15 error code guide
Bosch dishwasher error codes explained

steps: Turn the water supply off and unplug the dishwasher.
Mop up any visible water and check hose connections and the door seal.

The base tray sits under the machine: draining it (a commonly published step is to tilt the machine carefully to let the tray water out, and to dry the polystyrene float) may clear the code — but it does not fix the leak.
Dry the area, restore water and power, and run a short cycle while watching for drips.
If E15 returns, water is still reaching the tray. The leak source must be found and repaired.
codes.title: Leak detected — water in the base tray

call_tech: E24 persists with a clear hose, high loop, and clean filter
The drain pump makes no sound or hums without pumping
Water backs up into the sink
causes: A clogged or kinked drain hose
A missing or sagging high loop under the sink
A blocked garbage disposal connection (including a knock-out plug never removed on a new disposal)
A dirty sump filter
A drain pump problem (see also E25)
checks: Look at the drain hose under the sink for kinks
Check the high loop — the hose should rise up under the sink before going down to the drain
Check the garbage disposal connection for a blockage
Remove and inspect the sump filter in the bottom of the tub

faqs.a: Both are drain faults. E24 points to the drain circuit generally (hose, filter, connection). E25 points more specifically at the drain pump being blocked or jammed.
faqs.q: What is the difference between E24 and E25?

faqs.a: Yes — a common one. If the disposal's dishwasher knock-out plug was never removed, the dishwasher cannot drain into it at all.
faqs.q: Can a new garbage disposal cause E24?

codes.meaning: The dishwasher is not draining correctly. Water stays in the bottom of the tub at the end of the cycle, or the machine stops mid-cycle because the drain circuit is not clearing water fast enough.
codes.reset: A power cycle clears a one-off glitch, but a blocked hose or filter will bring E24 straight back.
codes.safety: Unplug before reaching into the sump or touching the drain pump area. Keep the water supply off if you disconnect any hose.

sources.label: Bosch dishwasher E15 error code guide (includes E24/E25 table)
Bosch dishwasher error codes explained

steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Check the drain hose for kinks and confirm the high loop is in place.
If connected to a garbage disposal, check that connection is clear (and, on a new disposal, that the knock-out plug was removed).
Remove the sump filter from the bottom of the tub, rinse it clean, and refit it.
Restore power and run a short cycle to test draining.
codes.title: Drain error — the dishwasher is not draining

call_tech: The impeller is broken or the pump shaft wobbles
The pump makes no sound at all when it should drain
E25 returns with a clean, correctly covered pump
causes: Debris at the pump (glass shards, seeds, bones, small objects)
A loose or incorrectly seated white pump cover
A damaged impeller or a failing pump
checks: Remove the sump filter and look down at the pump area
Check whether the white pump cover is loose or lifted
Look for visible debris around the impeller

faqs.a: E24 is the general drain fault (hose, filter, connection). E25 points at the pump itself being blocked or jammed.
faqs.q: What is the difference between E24 and E25?

faqs.a: Usually not — the white cover lifts off by hand on most Bosch models. Your manual shows the exact method for your model.
faqs.q: Do I need tools to open the pump cover?

codes.meaning: The drain pump is blocked or jammed — usually by debris at the pump, or because the pump cover is loose. The dishwasher cannot pump water out, so the cycle stops.
codes.reset: A reset cannot clear a jammed impeller. The debris must come out first.
codes.safety: Unplug before opening the pump cover. Wear gloves — broken glass in the sump is the most common injury in this job.

sources.label: Bosch dishwasher E15 error code guide (includes E24/E25 table)
Bosch dishwasher error codes explained

steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Remove the filter from the bottom of the tub and scoop out standing water.
Pop off the white plastic pump cover and remove any debris around the impeller. Work carefully — glass is common here; wear gloves.
Reseat the pump cover firmly until it clicks.
Refit the filter, restore power, and run a short cycle to test draining.
codes.title: Drain pump blocked — the pump impeller is jammed

call_tech: The duct is long, built in, or you cannot reach the full path
The code returns after a full cleaning
There is a burning smell — stop using the dryer immediately
Note: on gas dryers, a d80 code can also indicate a lack of gas supply
causes: Lint buildup in the exhaust duct
A crushed, kinked, or damaged exhaust hose
A long duct run, or one with many elbows, that traps lint
A blocked outside vent hood (lint, debris, or a stuck flap)
Foil or plastic ducting instead of rigid or semi-rigid metal
checks: Clean the lint filter — wash it with soap if it feels coated, and dry it fully
Look at the exhaust hose for crushing or kinks
Check the outside vent hood: the flap should open freely when the dryer runs
Run a timed dry with an empty drum and feel for strong airflow outside

faqs.a: They are the same warning at different severities: roughly 75%, 80%, 90%, and 95% exhaust blockage. d80 gives you time to clean; d90 and d95 mean stop and clean now.
faqs.q: What is the difference between d75, d80, d90, and d95?

faqs.a: Clean the lint filter after every load, and deep-clean the vent system every 6–12 months — more often with long ducts or heavy use.
faqs.q: How often should I clean the vent system?

codes.meaning: The dryer's Flow Sense system has detected that the exhaust duct is about 80% blocked. The dryer still runs, but drying takes longer and the machine runs hotter. d75 means 75% blocked, d90 means 90%, and d95 means 95% — the higher the number, the more urgent the blockage. These are safety warnings, not dryer malfunctions.
codes.reset: There is no reset for Flow Sense codes — they clear when airflow is restored. If the code returns after cleaning, the blockage is deeper in the duct, or the blower fan is faulty.
codes.safety: Reduced airflow is a fire risk if ignored — lint plus heat is the classic dryer fire combination. Do not keep running a dryer showing d90 or d95. On gas dryers, shut the gas off before disconnecting anything.

sources.label: LG USA support — dryer error code list (official)
LG support — Flow Sense warning d80/d90/d95 troubleshooting (official)

steps: Unplug the dryer. If it is a gas dryer, shut the gas off as well.
Remove and clean the lint filter. If it feels coated, wash it with soap and water and dry it completely before refitting.
Disconnect the exhaust hose and check it for kinks, crushing, and lint. Vacuum lint out of the hose.
Brush or vacuum lint along the full vent path. If the duct is long or inaccessible, hire a vent cleaning specialist — they have the right tools.
Clear the outside vent hood and confirm the flap opens freely.
Reconnect everything, use rigid or semi-rigid metal duct where possible, and run a timed dry with an empty drum. Strong airflow outside means the blockage is cleared.
codes.title: Flow Sense warning — the exhaust vent is about 80% blocked

tagline: Understand appliance error codes, explore possible causes, and follow practical troubleshooting steps.
